conventions.commits: Conventional Commits with DCO sign-off (Signed-off-by) and GPG signing (git commit -S --signoff), per CONTRIBUTING.md L25 and L62-L72; recent commits all carry Signed-off-by.
conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] modules in each languages/*.rs (queries_compile, element match, inheritance, defuse write site, empty file); registry table test in languages/mod.rs; extension tests in lang.rs; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in.
conventions.linting: cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used, undocumented_unsafe_blocks; clippy.toml msrv 1.98.0; REUSE compliance.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec and never panic in non-test code; query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError in parser.rs; tests use expect() with messages (exempt via cfg_attr).

patterns: Each language handler is a module under languages/ exporting ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str constants (java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs).
Registry wiring is two match arms in languages/mod.rs (get_language_info and get_ts_language) plus a pub mod line and an EXTENSION_MAP row in lang.rs (css integration).
extract_inheritance handlers take (&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> and prefix results with 'extends' or 'implements' (java.rs); swift.rs walks child(i) by kind rather than by field name.
Element name capture names are contractual: parser_elements.rs matches function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name, type_name.
Call sites use capture name 'call' and the captured node text is the callee (parser_elements.rs L495-L500).
Import capture 'import_path' feeds extract_imports_from_node, whose fallback arm stores the full node text as the module string (non-Rust languages).
DEFUSE capture prefixes write., writeread., read. are classified in parser_elements.rs L868-L885; reads at the same byte offset as a write are de-duplicated.
Inline unit tests use a local parse_<lang> helper and a StreamingIterator-based query loop (java.rs, swift.rs).
enclosing_function_name already lists function_definition and method_declaration (parser_elements.rs L435-L441), so PHP caller attribution needs no change.
supported_file_ext_pattern is generated from EXTENSION_MAP, so a new extension needs no schema edit.

related_issues.relevance: The task issue. Labels: enhancement, testing, feature, feat. No comments. Body states the maintainers implement this in-house and external PRs will be closed.

constraints: Issue #1864 states external pull requests are not accepted; this Scout output is for internal planning only.

Scope excludes extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, trait use resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace alias import, and .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5 extensions.
Mixed HTML and PHP must parse with zero ERROR nodes, so the grammar must be LANGUAGE_PHP; LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY's php_only/src/node-types.json contains no 'text' node (verified).

New Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old; tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 was tagged 2026-11-19 (8 days before the 2026-11-27 run date), so it passes only narrowly; crates.io publish date not independently verified.

Workspace tree-sitter is 0.27.1; tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends on tree-sitter-language 0.1 and dev-depends on tree-sitter 0.27, so the Language conversion is expected to be compatible but must be confirmed by compiling.

DEFUSE_QUERY has no production caller: extract_def_use is cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)) (parser_elements.rs ~L838-L850), so it is required for the issue's five-constant scope and for test parity, not for runtime paths.
Non-test code must avoid unwrap/expect/unsafe under workspace lints.
test_coverage: Affected areas are covered by inline tests in java.rs, swift.rs and css.rs (query compile, element match, inheritance, empty file), the registry table test in languages/mod.rs (lists css, yaml, markdown, tsx, fortran but not swift, java, or kotlin), extension tests in lang.rs (swift and fortran rows present; no php), and integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/integration_tests.rs (analyze_module on a temp .rs file). No PHP-related tests exist.

approaches.name: A: Full Java-template handler with all five queries and registry wiring (recommended)
approaches.description: Add crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance (walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children). Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP. Set extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type to None (out of scope per #1864). Add tree-sitter-php to root and crate Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; add ("php","php") to EXTENSION_MAP and "php" to supported_languages(); add pub mod php, the get_language_info arm (reference_query and import_query Some, defuse_query Some) and the get_ts_language arm; add php to the registry table test as ("php", true, true); add README entry; add inline tests and one integration test file.
pros: Matches the issue's five-constant scope and acceptance criteria exactly
Follows the java.rs and swift.rs templates, so reviewers recognize the shape
Inline DEFUSE test can mirror test_defuse_query_write_site with symbol 'z'
No new architecture; only one new handler file
cons: DEFUSE_QUERY and REFERENCE_QUERY have no runtime consumer beyond tests and extract_references
Requires a compile-verified query set since no tree-sitter-php query file was run locally
Cargo.lock change needs a new registry entry and the 7-day age check passes only narrowly

approaches.name: B: Minimal handler without DEFUSE_QUERY or REFERENCE_QUERY
approaches.description: Same as A but set defuse_query: None and reference_query: None in the registry arm, and omit DEFUSE_QUERY and REFERENCE_QUERY constants. Keep ELEMENT, CALL, IMPORT and extract_inheritance.
pros: Smallest handler file and fewest tests to write
Registry supports None for defuse_query (parser.rs L159 only compiles when Some)
cons: Violates the issue's explicit five-constant requirement and the DEFUSE acceptance intent
Breaks the test-parity convention used by java, swift, css-free languages and kotlin
Leaves def-use analysis unavailable for PHP if a consumer is restored

approaches.name: C: Split .php into pure-PHP and HTML-template handling via LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY
approaches.description: Parse .php with tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for speed and add a pre-pass that strips or segments inline HTML before parsing.
pros: Pure PHP files parse without the text node
cons: LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY's node-types.json has no 'text' node (verified), so inline HTML cannot be represented; fails the zero-ERROR acceptance criterion
Requires new segmentation logic and offset mapping, outside the registry pattern
Highest complexity for no stated benefit

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies the issue's five-constant scope and acceptance criteria while following the java.rs and swift.rs registry pattern. LANGUAGE_PHP is required (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) because the HTML-template criterion needs the text node. DEFUSE_QUERY is required by the issue scope and the test-parity convention, not by a production path.

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: php/src/grammar.json rule class_declaration (from tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, fetched via gh api) is a SEQ of: optional FIELD attributes; REPEAT of _modifier; keyword class; FIELD name (SYMBOL name); CHOICE of SYMBOL base_clause or BLANK; CHOICE of SYMBOL class_interface_clause or BLANK; FIELD body (SYMBOL declaration_list). The walk: (1) child_by_field_name('name') gives the class name. (2) base_clause is NOT a field; it is an unfielded child, so iterate child(i) and match kind == 'base_clause'. base_clause rule is SEQ of keyword extends followed by _name, then REPEAT of comma and _name; _name is hidden and resolves to name, qualified_name or relative_name, so the extends targets are the named children of base_clause with kinds name, qualified_name, relative_name. (3) class_interface_clause is likewise an unfielded child of class_declaration; rule is SEQ of keyword implements then _name list, so implements targets are its named children with the same three kinds. (4) php/src/node-types.json confirms: class_declaration fields are only attributes, body, name (no superclass or interfaces field, unlike Java); base_clause children are name, qualified_name, relative_name; class_interface_clause children are the same. interface_declaration uses base_clause for multiple extends; enum_declaration uses class_interface_clause (and an optional primitive_type after ':' for backed enums); trait_declaration has neither clause.
